answer: Shared Operator Liability Pool. Each identity must declare an operator; identities sharing an operator draw from one collateral pool. Any confirmed duplicate (same controller keys or correlated timing) slashes the pool, so an attacker who lets identities wander across many keys still loses one shared deposit per operator. The pool must cover a jade-level reserve that scales with identity count, and a dune-sized fee per added identity, making N fakes cost N deposits, not one.
